meaning: Pico Boulevard is a street in Los Angeles.

line: My jewels is custom made, but I didn’t go to Kay
vault_lines: My jewels is custom made, but I didn't go to Kay
meaning: Kay Jewelers is an American jewelery chain that specialises in engagement and wedding rings, diamonds, charms and other types of jewlery. By having custom made jewelery, Amine let’s it be known that he has unique pieces made for his own pleasure – not something others could get.

line: In LA like my name Dre
vault_lines: In LA like my name Dre
meaning: Dr. Dre has built an empire for himself off the back of a successful career in the music industry, using his experience to work with record labels and then in entrepreneurship with the famous Beats by Dre. Dre of course is a native of Compton, California, a city in Southern Los Angeles where it’d be likely to find him.

line: Gelato and Percocets one of my habits
vault_lines: Gelato and Percocets one of my habits
meaning:
Gelato is a milk and sugar-base ice cream that in reality, is more like sorbet. It is known for its refreshing taste and comparatively low-fat content, though is also considerably more expensive. Gelato is also a term used for a strain of weed common in the US, so Herbo could be alluding to a recreational use of Marijuana.

Percocets, often referred to as “percs”, are a drug known for having several side effects and possible health risks. However, it can also cause euphoria and make the user feel good, so Herbo does have reason to use it.

line: This a Hellcat, 700 horsepower on that bitch You can’t hear me slide
vault_lines: This a Hellcat, 700 horsepower on that bitch
meaning:
Dodge took the world by storm when they unveiled their Dodge Challenger SRT Hellcat which quickly became popular for its insanely fast drag-times and comparatively cheap price. Boasting a 6.2 liter V8 supercharged to produce 707 horsepower and 650 pound-feet of torque, the Hellcat is both extremely fast and awfully loud.



It is unclear as to what is meant when saying “you can’t hear me slide” though chances are if he were driving one, you’d most certainly hear it.

line: You don’t ever see me ridin’ no Acura
vault_lines: You don't ever see me ridin' no Acura
meaning:
Acura is the luxury branch of Japanese brand Honda famous for their production of the Acura NSX, one of 2018’s most underrated supercars.

https://images.genius.com/9633ea667371b8cc8e9c9cb2befd832a.1000x664x1.webp

Despite their flagship NSX being a great car, Amine refers to the whole brand in a negative light for their less impressive family cars. Average design, expensive pricing and poor quality have made many people critique the brand in general, whose efforts seem solely based on their modern NSX model.

line: Bitch I’m fresh as hell, these Amiri’s now Mike Amiri DM’d me on the ‘Gram Told me do the Amiri challenge Mixin’ Amiri jeans and jacket with the Guwop shirt That’s the Amiri balance
vault_lines: Bitch I'm fresh as hell, these Amiri’s now
meaning:
Amiri is a popular brand in the US that’s been billed as “making Rock n Roll cool again.” The ‘Gram refers to Instagram, a photo-sharing social media platform— Mike Amiri’s account can be viewed here.

The “Amiri Challenge” doesn’t seem to actually exist though several YouTubers have released reviews and comparisons on Amiri products.

The Guwop shirt could refer to rapper Gucci Mane and his merchandise, or simply to Gucci, arguably the world’s most recognisable high-fashion brand.

line: Independent like my first name Webbie
vault_lines: Independent like my first name Webbie
meaning: Webbie is another Louisiana rapper who is in fact signed to Lil Boosie’s label Trill Entertainment. Independent is Webbie’s 2007 hit that peaked at no.9 on the Billboard Hot 100 and so Amine references him here, calling himself Independent and alluding to Webbie’s song.

line: We don’t ever love thots or the groupies That’s word to my OG Boosie
vault_lines: We don't ever love thots or the groupies
meaning:
OG Boosie, also known as Boosie Badazz and formerly Lil Boosie is a Louisiana rapper who doesn’t seem to have connections with Amine at all. However, Boosie was called out for having slept with a groupie who then proceeded to post a nude photo to Twitter of the two of them. It can be found here. (NSFW)

Boosie received significant backlash for this, being accused of serious thirst levels and for messing around too much. He then received backlash for signing a girl’s underwear backstage as seen here.

line: I’m out here with Topanga like I’m white and my name Cory
vault_lines: I'm out here with Topanga like I'm white and my name Cory
meaning:
“Boy Meets World” was a TV sitcom that aired from 1993-2000 and recounted the life of Cory Matthews who struggles to balance the several aspects of his teenage life. Topanga is his true love in the show, and together they tackle life’s experiences for 7 seasons before the show came to an end in 2000.

Amine is suggesting that he’s got a girl he’s madly in love with by his side, as if he was Cory.

line: I’m starin’ at the window of this Buick (yuh!)
vault_lines: I'm starin' at the window of this Buick (yuh!)
meaning:
Buick may be scoffed at as a B-rate car company nowadays, but the company has a historic relationship with rap. The 1973 Buick Regal is referenced in Rae Sremmurd’s “Black Beatles”:

I’m a fuckin' black Beatle, cream seats in the Regal

It was also mentioned in Lil Uzi Vert’s song “Enemies” and even Kendrick Lamar’s “Alright”. This Hypebeast article discusses the Regal and other common cars in rap.

Aminé’s references Maryland rapper Rico Nasty, and Chicago rapper G Herbo, both of whom are also featured throughout ONEPOINTFIVE.  Rico appears on “SUGARPARENTS” for a hook and verse all about money, Herbo features on this track and Aminé is stating that he has the swagger of both of them.

In addition, this is a reference to the song “Swervo” by Herbo and Soutside.
